title: 2025-11-20 Eval & Quality Monitoring Demo with MapleHealth
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-20 15:00 PST, Duration: 48 mins. Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair (Redwood); Evan Kim, Sara Patel, Miguel Torres, Aisha Rana (MapleHealth).

Summary (auto): Redwood demo of Eval/Quality Monitoring (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) focusing on API, Console, and Optimize. Customer asks about alerting thresholds, integration with existing test suites, and private deployment constraints. Next steps agreed: share trial prompt-set template, security docs, and schedule a pilot benchmark.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya, our SE. Quick round robin?
[00:08] Evan Kim: Evan here, CTO at MapleHealth. Sara and Miguel are on from ML and eng. Aisha PM.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. We'll demo Eval and the quality monitoring flows — prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons across model variants and quantization.
[00:22] Sara Patel: High level right now we're doing inference in-house on g4dn and some CPU fallbacks; we ship clinical summaries and patient triage suggestions, so precision and auditability are huge.
[00:34] Miguel Torres: We're particularly worried about silent regressions when we push model or prompt changes, and about latency spikes during peak hours.
[00:42] Priya Nair: Totally. We'll show how Redwood's Console ties API telemetry to evals. For example, you can attach a prompt-set to a route, get per-prompt pass/fail, and trigger regression alerts if the F1 drops or hallucination rate rises.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: Quick note — some of the transcript badges might say K V cache or K V cache when we talk about KV cache, apologies if that shows up odd.
[01:05] Evan Kim: Also curious about how this interacts with our CI. We run nightly tests and have a separate MLOps pipeline. Can we hook alerts into Slack and into our JIRA?
[01:15] Priya Nair: Yes — out of the box we have webhooks, and we can forward alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or a webhook for a JIRA automation. You can also export eval deltas as CSV or connect via API.
[01:28] Sara Patel: Walk us through the prompt-set format. We have several templates and a bunch of expected outputs — some graded, some free-text.
[01:36] Priya Nair: Sure. Prompt sets are JSONL-like, each row is a case with input, expected_output, tags, tolerance levels. In Console you can upload a CSV or use our API to push prompt sets. We'll show an example now.
[01:50] [screen share noise]
[02:02] Priya Nair: Here in Console the eval tab shows prompt sets. You can create checkpoints (baseline) and then run A/B comparisons between model v1 and v2 or quantized variants. We compute metrics like exact match, BLEU, and custom validators you write. Note — custom validators are run in a sandbox; they can be offloaded to your environment if you prefer.
[02:28] Miguel Torres: Can we run validators that call our internal services? Some of our checks need access to clinical ontologies.
[02:34] Priya Nair: Yes, via our secure runner in Private deployments, or via webhooks for Hosted but behind a VPC connector. For on-prem we can integrate directly.
[02:45] Evan Kim: How are regression alerts configured? Do we get alerted on absolute metric drops or relative deltas?
[02:51] Jordan Lee: Both. You can set absolute thresholds and delta-based alerts (e.g., >5% drop in F1 vs baseline). Alerts can be scoped per-prompt-tag so noisy prompts don't spam you.
[03:05] Aisha Rana: Is there a concept of canary rollout for prompts/versions? We want to test with 5% of traffic first.
[03:12] Priya Nair: Yes — rollout controls tie into our routing. You can do canary traffic splits, A/B compare outputs in real time, and get drift/regression signals.
[03:22] Sara Patel: Latency — you mentioned quantized variants. We care about p95 tail latency for patient-facing pathways. How do you recommend balancing quantization and quality?
[03:33] Priya Nair: Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles by workload. We run simulated evals: compare a standard FP16 model vs 4-bit quant; it reports per-scenario metric deltas and cost savings. You can then pin a model variant for a route with a fallback to a higher-fidelity model on errors or high-importance prompts.
[03:52] Miguel Torres: Any examples of regression alerts in the UI?
[03:56] [short pause]
[04:00] Priya Nair: Yes — demoing now. In the Alerts view you get a feed with the failing prompt-set, the offending metric, a small diff of outputs, and links to the request trace. You can also jump to the API logs to see the raw tokens, latency, and token cost.
[04:20] Evan Kim: Request trace — does that include full PII content? Our policy forbids storing PHI in logs.
[04:27] Jordan Lee: Good callout. For Hosted we have configurable redaction and retention. For Dedicated and Private you can disable request logging entirely or route logs to your KMS/HSM-protected store. We support field-level redaction and token-level avoidance, and SOC2 controls on the storage.
[04:48] Sara Patel: How do we run scheduled evals? We want nightly regression checks against the latest baseline.
[04:55] Priya Nair: You can schedule eval runs in Console or trigger via API from your CI. The job will run across the pinned models and store results; if thresholds are crossed it creates a regression alert.
[05:08] Miguel Torres: If an alert fires, can we auto-rollback to previous prompt or model?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Yes — we have automated fallback policies. On regression we can automatically switch traffic to a previous model or route, or disable a problematic prompt set.
[05:22] Aisha Rana: Integration cost — curious about pricing for eval runs.
[05:27] Jordan Lee: Eval runs are metered by token and compute — we can share a pricing sheet. For pilots we usually provide credits to run initial baselines.
[05:35] [09:30 — intermittent screen demo continues; timestamps every ~30–60s from here to match duration] 
[09:30] Priya Nair: Example prompt set: triage symptom -> recommended next step. We'll run a quick A/B: baseline model (redwood-open-2024) vs tuned prompt + quant 4-bit.
[10:00] Priya Nair: Results: quant variant reduced latency p95 by ~30% but showed a 3.2% drop in exact match for this prompt-set. You can set a delta threshold to ignore <5% drops or to alert immediately.
[11:15] Sara Patel: That delta is acceptable for some templates but not for others. We need per-template tolerance.
[11:22] Priya Nair: Exactly — you can tag prompts and set per-tag thresholds.
[12:05] Miguel Torres: How do we validate hallucination? Some outputs are plausible but incorrect; we want validators that check against canonical data.
[12:12] Priya Nair: Use custom validators or fuzzy matching against your canonical datasets. We also support human-in-the-loop review flows where low-confidence items are queued for annotators.
[13:01] Evan Kim: About data residency — we have EU patients, and some data can't leave region. Can we pin eval storage to eu-west?
[13:08] Jordan Lee: Yes — for Dedicated and Private you can choose region and storage residency. Hosted supports EU regions with residency controls and contractual addendums.
[13:20] Sara Patel: Security — can you walk through SSO and audit logs?
[13:24] Priya Nair: We support SAML/Okta SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with granular roles, and immutable audit logs. For Private deployments audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM. Note — sometimes our transcript auto-keywords show S A M L as sam el, so apologies.
[13:41] Aisha Rana: Competitors — are you comparing this to any other platform?
[13:45] Jordan Lee: Many customers run in-house or use general LLM endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic), or inference vendors like Replicate/Cohere. We focus on production-grade observability and rollout controls.
[14:00] Sara Patel: Any limitations on prompt-set size or cron frequency?
[14:05] Priya Nair: Large sets are fine; we chunk and batch. For huge corpora we recommend scheduled sampling and smart bucketing to keep costs manageable.
[14:22] Miguel Torres: API details — can you show how to attach a prompt set to an API route?
[14:28] Priya Nair: Sure — via the Routes page or the REST API: POST /routes/{id}/evals with a prompt_set_id. Then responses are correlated with logs.
[14:40] [demo continues; screen: compare outputs and diff view] 
[16:00] Priya Nair: Notice here the A/B output diff: color-coded tokens, and a small metric summary. You can click into the request trace to see token-level latency and cost.
[16:20] Evan Kim: Does the diff show prompt tokens too? We sometimes mutate prompts at runtime.
[16:25] Priya Nair: Yes — request traces include final prompt and generation. You can enable masked logging to redact PII from prompt content.
[16:40] Sara Patel: For our clinical use, we need a human review queue and a way to retrain prompts based on feedback.
[16:45] Priya Nair: You can surface low-confidence items to a review queue; annotators can label and that becomes new training or new prompt cases, which you re-run in evals.
[17:10] Miguel Torres: Any gotchas with private deployments? E.g., network egress or KMS integration.
[17:16] Jordan Lee: Private has network restrictions: we can run controllers in your VPC; for KMS we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSMs. You keep key control.
[17:30] Evan Kim: Benchmarks — can Redwood run a pilot to compare our tuned model vs your open models?
[17:35] Jordan Lee: Yes — typical pilot: you send prompt sets, we run against multiple model variants and quant profiles, produce a benchmark spreadsheet and dashboards. We'll provide credits for the initial run.
[18:02] Sara Patel: Timeline — we want to pilot in the next 4–6 weeks. Who's needed?
[18:07] Jordan Lee: For a pilot we need: a technical contact (to share prompt sets and CI hooks), security contact (for privacy/agreements), and an exec sponsor. We can run a week-long baseline and a two-week A/B pilot.
[18:25] Aisha Rana: Cost and contracts — our procurement asks for SOC2, DPA, and security questionnaires.
[18:31] Jordan Lee: We will send SOC2 and our security packet; for Dedicated/Private we offer enterprise contracts and DPAs.
[18:40] [demo wrap-up, actionable items]
[19:00] Priya Nair: Quick recap: Prompt-set upload, schedule evals or run via API, set per-tag thresholds, get regression alerts, and configure rollouts/fallbacks.
[19:12] Evan Kim: Sounds good. A few clarifying Qs — if we set automatic rollback, is there a cooldown window?
[19:18] Priya Nair: Yes, rollback policies support cooldowns and manual overrides.
[19:25] Sara Patel: Can you demo the A/B summary export?
[19:28] Priya Nair: Export produces CSV with per-prompt metrics and diffs; we can also push to S3 or your internal storage.
[19:40] Miguel Torres: For our CI, we'll want a webhook payload sample.
[19:44] Jordan Lee: We'll include that in follow-up materials.
[20:02] Aisha Rana: Anything else on privacy?
[20:06] Jordan Lee: We'll include field-level redaction docs and retention policy options.
[20:15] [wrap next steps and assign owners]
[20:20] Jordan Lee: Great — recap and next steps coming. Thanks everyone.

End transcript.
summary: Redwood demoed Eval/Quality Monitoring (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) across API, Console, and Optimize. MapleHealth has concerns about silent regressions, latency, PHI in logs, and regional data residency. Agreed pilot in 4–6 weeks. Redwood to send trial prompt-set template, security docs, pricing, and webhook samples.
next_steps: Jordan Lee to send pilot proposal and pricing sheet (includes eval credits)
Priya Nair to share prompt-set template and API webhook examples
Jordan to send SOC2 and security packet
Schedule pilot kickoff in 4 weeks; possible dates proposed via email
